prompt:
Deliverable: One production website hero background image, 1536 x 1024 pixels, landscape 3:2. A complete standalone cinematic night-sea still life, ready to place behind real HTML text. No text. No UI. No letters or numbers anywhere in the image.

Reference-image roles:
Image 1 is the selected website mockup and the primary visual reference. Preserve its exquisite moonlit deep-teal ocean world, dark mountain horizon, restrained brass highlights, Going Merry miniature, water-filled circular platform, field journal and glass/brass compass. Use its upper hero scene as the style and composition reference. Remove all interface elements, portrait, navigation, page copy, buttons, labels, dividers, project thumbnail and lower content section. This output is an image asset rather than a webpage mockup.
Image 2 is the Going Merry ship identity reference. Preserve the recognizable sheep figurehead, wooden hull, white rails, large cream square sail with the straw-hat skull-and-crossbones emblem, two small black flags and red-and-white striped rear sail. Give this ship the physically rich, beautifully lit miniature materials seen in Image 1. Keep one ship, one compass and one closed journal only.

Scene and composition:
Create one uninterrupted dark ocean extending across the entire image. The left 45 percent of the canvas is a calm, dark low-contrast negative-space region, clear of objects, bright reflections, and strong clouds; real webpage copy will occupy that region. On the right half, a shallow oval/circular dark patinated metal maritime worktable sits just above the water, extending from roughly x=720 to x=1500 and y=490 to y=910. Its interior includes a small patch of sea where the complete Going Merry is sailing, plus a small parchment chart, one aged canvas-bound closed journal, rope and a single precision glass/brass navigation compass on the right foreground. No brass nameplate, engraved words, written notes or letters on any object. The journal cover is plain with subtle worn binding; the parchment may show faint coastline linework but absolutely no text. The compass is built from glass, warm brass, a red needle and simple unlabeled tick marks; no numerals or cardinal letters.
The ship is the focal object, centered around x=1120, with its highest flag around y=245 and hull around y=630, within the right half of the scene. Show the entire ship and all flag tips with ample air around them. Keep the whole platform inside the image with a margin on the right and bottom. Slight low three-quarter camera angle, like Image 1, so the ship's sheep figurehead points toward lower left and the rear sail appears to its right. Avoid a top-down map composition. Do not enlarge the ship beyond the right-half object grouping.
One softly luminous full moon is behind the scene around x=1080, y=145, amid sparse soft clouds. Its restrained silver reflection stays behind the ship, mostly in the right half. Low distant mountainous islands form a soft horizontal silhouette around y=330. Very dark cyan ocean ripples and subtle localized caustics connect the object grouping to the sea. Keep the left half visually quieter than Image 1 for excellent readability with overlaid cream-white text.

Visual treatment:
Premium cinematic physically rendered miniature diorama, highly convincing linen, aged wood, patinated brass, clear glass and water materials. Cool moonlight overhead, small warm ship-cabin glow, gentle brass highlights, deep atmospheric shadow, softly volumetric air. Palette centers on deep ocean #061a22, muted teal #12323b, warm linen cream and subdued antique gold. Match the moody realism and refined oceanic fantasy of Image 1. No neon, purple, glowing sci-fi lines, sparkles, particles, extra scenery or extra characters. Preserve rich yet calm contrast, without a flat blue wash or a cartoon illustration look.
The left edge, lower edge and corners must naturally fall into nearly solid #061a22 darkness for seamless blending with a dark teal webpage. Do not add an obvious vignette frame or border. Keep all key objects sharp and subtly atmospheric; do not simulate motion blur. This is the resting visual for small-amplitude pointer parallax and gentle water lighting, so composition must tolerate a slight crop at the canvas edges while leaving every main object whole.

Invariants and exclusions:
Preserve the selected reference's nautical identity, ship proportions and material language. Change only from a webpage mockup into an independent uninterrupted hero-scene asset and adapt the framing to the specified negative space. Output exactly one complete scene. No text, no typography, no logo outside the requested straw-hat sail/flag identity, no watermarks, no signature, no UI, no navigation, no avatar, no header, no buttons, no inset panels, no split views, no labels, no caption, no title, no legible writing on journal, maps, compass or platform.
